papers.title_in_file: Efficient parametric frequency conversions in lithium niobate nanophotonic chips
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting a periodically poled lithium niobate nanowaveguide with SHG, DFG and SPDC photon-pair generation results.

assertions.value: The authors report a normalized SHG efficiency of over 2200%W −1cm−2 for a PPLN waveguide with 4 mm length and 4 µm period.
quotes: This corresponding to normalized SHG efﬁciency for this PPLN waveguide with 4 mm length and 4 µm period of over 2200%W −1cm−2.
assertions.reader_inference: A single device, one measurement; the value is a lower bound ('over').

assertions.value: The authors report measured on-chip pump power of 2.95 mW and second-harmonic power of 31.56 µW, from which the normalized SHG efficiency was obtained.
quotes: the measured on-chip pump power and SH power are 2.95 mW and 31.56 µW, respectively.

assertions.value: The authors state that the normalized SHG efficiency calculated with the actual waveguide parameters is more than 5, 000%W −1cm−2, and attribute the lower measured value to fabrication and poling tolerances.
assertions.anchor: Section II p.5; Section III.A p.7
quotes: calculated using the actual waveguide parameters is more than 5, 000%W −1cm−2.
We believe that lower measured normalized SHG efﬁciency compared to the theoretical prediction is primarily due to tolerances in device fabrication and poling process.
assertions.reader_inference: The attribution is a belief of the authors, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that their efficiency of 2200% W −1cm−2 is comparable to the record efficiency on nanophotonic PPLN, citing earlier work.
quotes: We observe high conversion efﬁciency of 2200% W −1cm−2, which is comparable to the record efﬁciency on nanophotonic PPLN

assertions.value: The authors report an optimized waveguide cross section with 500 nm height, 1850 nm top width and a 67◦ sidewall angle.
quotes: Figure 1(a) shows the optimized cross section of a LN nanowaveguide, with 500 nm in height, 1850 nm in the top width, and a 67◦ sidewall angle.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own device geometry in Section II.

assertions.value: The authors state that simulations determine a waveguide width and height giving subwavelength mode confinement and over 90% overlap of the interacting modes.
quotes: for subwavelength mode conﬁnement and over 90% overlap
assertions.reader_inference: The overlap is simulated; the measured profiles are described only as nearly identical.

assertions.value: The authors state that the required poling period for this geometry is about 4 µm.
quotes: The required poling period for this geometry is about 4 µm.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the design poling period in Section II.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguide is periodically poled for type-0 quasi-phase matching, each interacting light guided in a TE mode, to use the largest nonlinearity tensor d33 of the X-cut LN thin film.
quotes: we periodically pole the waveguide to realize type-0 quasi-phase matching
(QPM), with each interacting light guided in a TE mode to fully utilize the largest nonlinearity
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own design in Section II.

assertions.value: The authors report an X-cut LNOI wafer with a 500 nm thick LN thin film bonded on a 2-µm thermally grown silicon dioxide layer above a silicon substrate.
quotes: which is a 500 nm thick LN thin ﬁlm bonded on a 2-µm thermally grown silicon dioxide layer above a silicon substrate
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own fabrication substrate.

assertions.value: The authors report an intrinsic quality factor of about 2 × 106 (printed flat; two million) on a microring of similar geometry, and infer a propagation loss of about 0.15 dB/cm.
assertions.anchor: Section II p.6; Appendix A p.11
quotes: indicating the propagation loss is about 0.15 dB/cm.
The highest intrinsic Q ∼ 2 × 106 is achieved on a 80 µm radius microring with 2 µm width.
assertions.reader_inference: The ring has a 2 µm top width, not the 1850 nm of the PPLN guide, so the loss is for similar, not identical, geometry.

assertions.value: The authors report a broadband DFG response of more than 4.5 THz, limited only by the accessible laser wavelength, with the pump at the phase-matched wavelength around 766 nm at 0.1 mW peak power in the waveguide.
quotes: a broadband DFG response (> 4.5 THz) is observed, only limited by the accessible laser wavelength.
DFG spectrum when pump at the phase-matched wavelength around 766 nm at 0.1 mW peak power in the waveguide.
assertions.reader_inference: The true DFG bandwidth is not measured; 4.5 THz is a lower bound set by the laser.

assertions.value: The authors report a CAR value of 631 ± 210 at a photon production rate of 0.8 million pairs per second.
quotes: We observe a CAR value of 631 ± 210 at photon production rate of 0.8 million pairs per second
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract and conclusion round this to 'as high as 600'; the uncertainty (210) is a third of the value.

assertions.value: The authors report a brightness of 69 MHz/mW/nm, with 0.0069 mean photon number per gate at the quoted production rate.
quotes: corresponding to a brightness of 69 MHz/mW/nm
(= 0.0069 means photon number per gate)

assertions.value: The authors report detection with two synchronized gated InGaAs single photon detectors at 100 MHz repetition rate and 1 ns gate width, and two 200 GHz bandpass filters each with over 35 dB extinction ratio.
quotes: two synchronized, gated InGaAs single photon detectors with 100 MHz repetition rate and 1 ns gate width
two 200 GHz bandpass ﬁlters (each over 35 dB extinction ratio)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own measurement setup.

assertions.value: The authors report collection of the generated photon pairs into SMF-28 fiber with 70% coupling efficiency, which they attribute to the well-defined fundamental spatial mode.
quotes: collected into to a SMF-28 optical ﬁber with 70% coupling efﬁciency, achievable thanks to the well-deﬁned fundamental spatial mode of the nanowaveguide.

assertions.value: The authors report an SPDC pump that is a CW narrow-linewidth (<200 KHz) laser around 767 nm and a chip temperature stabilized at 34.5 ◦C with 0.1 ◦C accuracy.
quotes: CW narrow linewidth (<200 KHz) tunable laser around 767 nm
The temperature of the PPLN chip is stabilized at 34.5 ◦C by a heater with accuracy of 0.1 ◦C.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own measurement setup.

assertions.value: The authors report fiber-to-chip coupling losses of 4.3 dB per facet at 1550 nm and 5.4 dB per facet at 775 nm.
quotes: with losses of 4.3 dB per facet at 1550 nm and 5.4 dB per facet at 775 nm

assertions.value: The authors report that the coincidence rate increases linearly with photon production rate while the accidental-coincidence rate increases quadratically.
quotes: the coincidence rate increases linearly with photon production rate while the accidental-coincidence rate increases quadratically

assertions.value: The authors report spectral correlation measurements across nine signal-idler channel combinations, with coincidences observed only for particular signal-idler combinations.
quotes: We characterize the spectral correlations between nine combinations of the signal and idler wavelength channels
consistent photon coincidences were measured only for particular signal-idler combination
assertions.reader_inference: Only nine combinations are tested, bounded by the 25 GHz waveshaper bandwidth the authors cite.

assertions.value: The authors state that the strong frequency correlation is anticipated to extend over a broad wavelength range, as predicted by the observed DFG bandwidth.
quotes: the strong frequency correlation is anticipated to extend over a broad wavelength range as predicted by the observed DFG bandwidth

assertions.value: The authors state that the CAR value can be improved significantly by narrow spectral filtering, time-gating or mode-selective detection.
quotes: the CAR value can be improved signiﬁcantly by reducing the time-frequency detection modes by the means of narrow spectral ﬁltering, time-gating, or the mode selective detection

assertions.value: The authors state that the oscillation in the measured phase matching curve is caused by a Fabry-Perot cavity between the two polished facets, which anti-reflection coating could suppress.
quotes: The oscillatory measured phase matching curve in Fig. 3(a) is caused by the Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity formed between the two polished facets on both end of the waveguide

assertions.value: The authors state that triangle-shape teeth on one side of the electrode, with a rectangular grounded side, are used to maintain the poling quality and acceptable yield for a small poling period.
quotes: in order to maintain the poling quality and acceptable yield for a small poling period
we use triangle-shape teeth on one side of the electrode while the other side remains in a rectangular shape for grounding.

assertions.value: The authors state that birefringent and geometric-dispersion phase matching cannot access the d33 tensor, and that higher-order-mode phase matching suffers poor overlap between fundamental and higher-order modes.
quotes: the former cannot access the d33 tensor with the highest χ(2) susceptibility, while latter suffers the poor mode overlapping between the fundamental and higher-order modes

assertions.value: The authors state that simulation gives ks + ki ≈ 2kp over 1500-1600 nm, which lets the SHG phase matching identify the optimum SPDC pump wavelength.
quotes: we ﬁnd that ks + ki ≈ 2kp, over a wide bandwidth in telecom wavelengths (1500- 1600 nm)
allowing us to determine the optimum pump wavelength for SPDC

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the same PPLN nanowaveguide gives a bright wavelength-multiplexing source of correlated photon pairs via SPDC with CAR as high as 600.
quotes: we implemented a bright, wavelength multiplexing source of correlated photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down conversion
achieving coincidental-to-accidental ratios as high as 600

assertions.value: The authors state that the next steps involve incorporating other optical elements, such as electro-optical modulation and wavelength multiplexing, on the same lithium-niobate chip.
quotes: The next steps will involve incorporating other optical elements on the same lithium-niobate chip
